text:
Tessa Morgan: UI review time for Usage Insights (route list + route detail). Figma is updated: https://figma.com/file/ri-usage-insights/route-cost-drivers?node-id=212%3A1189

Tessa Morgan: Main questions:
1) Route list layout (columns + what’s sticky)
2) Model breakdown viz on route detail (chart/table)
3) Export button placement (list vs detail, and discoverability)

Alicia Perez: went through the latest frames. overall feels solid. biggest thing: the route list table is getting dense w/ filters + sparklines + 6 columns.

Paula Mendes: +1. also want to be sure we’re not hiding the “unknown route” story. support expects that to dominate for some folks.

Felix Schneider: fwiw implementation-wise: sticky first column + sticky header is doable but we need to be careful with horizontal scroll + virtualization.

Dylan Brooks: re density: we can probably drop one of the “unit cost” columns from the default view? keep it behind a column picker.

Tessa Morgan: currently default columns: Route, Total cost, Tokens (in/out/cached), p95 latency, Error rate, Trend sparkline.

Alicia Perez: tokens column is the one that’s visually loud. could it be a compact “Tokens” with tooltip breakdown (in/out/cached) instead of 3 numbers inline?

Felix Schneider: tooltip breakdown is easy. would keep the table narrower.

Paula Mendes: I’d rather not bury cached tokens entirely. finance folks keep asking “why did cost drop but tokens didn’t” and it’s usually caching.

Tessa Morgan: maybe: show “Tokens (billable / total)”? billable = in+out minus cached? (wording TBD)

Paula Mendes: careful w/ definition. cached token accounting varies depending on prefix cache. we’ve been saying “cached tokens” separate, not “free”.

Dylan Brooks: product-wise, simplest: a single tokens number shown, then a “cached %” pill.

Alicia Perez: yes. “Cached 32%” is scannable.

Tessa Morgan: ok. I can revise the tokens column to: “Total tokens” + a small secondary line “Cached 32%” (or pill). Then the breakdown lives on the detail page.

Svetlana Orlov: design systems note: secondary line in tables is allowed but needs consistent line height. also pills inside dense tables can hurt contrast if we’re not careful.

Tessa Morgan: got it. will keep it text-only secondary line unless we really need the pill.

Marissa Cole: jumping in—route list is the money shot, so it has to be skimmable. I’m aligned w/ “Total cost” + “Trend” + one performance metric. tokens can move to “optional columns” imo.

Paula Mendes: I’m ok with tokens as optional, as long as route detail makes it obvious.

Tessa Morgan: next: Route naming display. right now we truncate after 48 chars and show full on hover.

Felix Schneider: please keep hover for desktop but we need something for keyboard focus too. (a11y)

Alicia Perez: we can do “focus reveals full route in a popover” + `aria-describedby`.

Svetlana Orlov: yes, use the standard “OverflowText + Tooltip” component so it’s consistent.

Tessa Morgan: noted.

Tessa Morgan: model breakdown viz on route detail: I mocked stacked bar (cost by model variant) + table below. alt option was treemap.

Alicia Perez: treemap looks cool but feels harder to read and not super accessible. stacked bar + table is safer.

Dylan Brooks: +1. stacked bar also maps nicely to “what changed” if we show two bars (current vs prior).

Paula Mendes: do we need to show fallback model explicitly? like “requested model” vs “served model”? edge case but it came up in eng.

Felix Schneider: backend will return served model and optionally requested model (if available). showing both might confuse.

Tessa Morgan: what if the table has “Model” (served) and an info icon when it differs from requested? maybe a small “fallback” tag.

Paula Mendes: love the “fallback tag”. and a tooltip: “Requests to X were served by Y due to capacity/policy.”

Marissa Cole: agree but keep it subtle. we don’t want every customer thinking something is wrong.

Alicia Perez: for the stacked bar legend, please keep to max 6 models and then “Other”. otherwise legend explodes.

Felix Schneider: we already have “top N + other” logic on the API side planned. can align N=6.

Tessa Morgan: ok.

Tessa Morgan: export button placement: currently on route list top-right (“Export report”). In route detail, there’s also an export in the kebab menu.

Paula Mendes: having both seems fine. list export = filtered report across routes. detail export = scoped to one route.

Dylan Brooks: I’d prefer no kebab for something as important as export. can we place “Export” next to the date picker on detail?

Alicia Perez: +1. kebab hides it. esp bc this feature is being built partly for finance workflows.

Svetlana Orlov: UI consistency: actions next to date range is standard in Console. we have an “Actions” dropdown pattern.

Tessa Morgan: ok: route detail will have date range picker left, then “Compare to prior” toggle, then “Export” as a button (or actions dropdown if we add more later).

Felix Schneider: heads up: export is async job for larger ranges. we need UI states: “Generating…” + toast + download ready.

Paula Mendes: and audit logging requirement. maybe include a small line in the modal: “Exports are audit logged.”

Tessa Morgan: yes, I’ll add copy to the confirm modal.

Marissa Cole: also consider: export should respect the current filters (env/region/deployment mode). call that out so users trust it.

Alicia Perez: for the list page export, modal should show the exact filter summary, like: “Last 7 days · prod · us-east · Hosted API”.

Felix Schneider: we can easily pass the filter object to the modal summary.

Tessa Morgan: awesome. last thing: empty states. if no route tag, we show “Unknown route” row at top with guidance.

Paula Mendes: can we also show an inline CTA “Learn how to set route identifiers” linking to docs.

Alicia Perez: yes. and maybe a dismissible info banner above table: “Routes are derived from SDK/gateway. Set `route` to reduce ‘Unknown’.”

Svetlana Orlov: banner component exists; needs to be non-blocking + collapsible.

Tessa Morgan: cool. I’ll update frames accordingly and tag you all for final check.

Dylan Brooks: thanks. once updated, can you also mark which columns are default vs optional? helps us implement column chooser.

Tessa Morgan: will do.

Paula Mendes: :thumbsup: please also sanity check that the “Cached %” language is consistent w docs. I’ll sync w Wei/Elliot.

Tessa Morgan: :thumbsup: follow-up: I’ll push a Figma update by EOD and drop link here.

Alicia Perez: :eyes: (also pls ensure color contrast on the stacked bar segments; some of the palette is too light)

Svetlana Orlov: +1, use DS categorical palette (avoid gray-on-white for “Other”).

Tessa Morgan: yep. will switch to DS palette + add patterns/labels for a11y where possible.

Felix Schneider: from eng side, if we keep it to stacked bar + table, we’re good. treemap would be a lot of custom code.

Marissa Cole: aligned. let’s ship the readable version.

Tessa Morgan: updated link w revisions (tokens secondary line + export on detail + actions near date picker): https://figma.com/file/ri-usage-insights/route-cost-drivers?node-id=212%3A2098

Paula Mendes: looks better. export placement is much more obvious now.

Felix Schneider: +1. I’ll mirror the filter summary in the export modal.

Alicia Perez: model breakdown is clean. “Other” is good. fallback tag is subtle.

Tessa Morgan: great. closing this thread unless more feedback comes in.
